prior_passes.notes: Argaam.com (already GEM's own Status[ref] for this row) independently confirms the GASCO-built 37 km / 12-inch line and states its purpose as delivering gas to 'two sugar and paper factories' and residential Edfu — this corroborates (2nd independent source, alongside Youm7 2022) the prior-suggestion's characterization of Edfu city as the delivery/terminal end. Youm7 (2025) and Elbalad confirm Egypt Gas Company's LOCAL distribution build-out around Edfu/Kom Ombo/Nasr al-Nuba markaz (a different infrastructure layer — low-pressure household/industrial distribution fed off this GASCO transmission spur), which is consistent with, but does not itself pin down, the transmission-line trunk tie-in. I could not find any source (Arabic or English) that names the specific valve-room or km-point where the 37 km line leaves the Dahshour–Aswan ('Upper Egypt') trunk — Kom Ombo is the best-supported bounding candidate (documented pressure-reduction/metering hub in that corridor) but is NOT itself confirmed as the tie-in, and Kom Ombo–Edfu is only ~15–20 km by road versus the sheet's 37 km, so treat 'near Kom Ombo' as a loose bound, not a fix. Recommend leaving this at ROUTE_PARTIAL (corridor-only, no two-point candidate) pending a GASCO network map or tender document naming the tie-in station explicitly. RouteAccuracy should stay capped at 'low' per the source ladder rules.

=== (b) EDFU-SIDE DELIVERY POINT — REFINED ===
Geocoded the Edfu sugar factory via Overpass/OSM: node 13622439309, name='مصنع السكر بادفو' (lit. 'the sugar factory at Edfu'), tagged place=village at 25.0432598N/32.8523728E — a distinct settlement 7.6km NNW of Edfu city center (24.9781N/32.8749E), added to OSM 2026-03-06 by a local mapper (user Ashraf714031). This is a real, named place — factory-adjacent worker villages carrying the factory's name are a common Egyptian OSM pattern. Straight-line distance from this node to the GEM-mapped trunk's nearest-approach point supplied by the main session (32.56065E/24.83748N — a computed geometric fact, NOT a citable source, used only to aim the search) is 37.27km, an almost exact match to GEM's stated 37km pipe length — a materially better fit than the city-center pin's 35.34km. No OSM feature exists yet for the paper/pulp factory itself, but almasryalyoum (2275932) independently confirms an actively-operating 'مصنع لب الورق بأدفو' (Edfu pulp & paper factory) that sources bagasse directly from the Edfu sugar factory and was, as of that article, negotiating a natural-gas price cut with the Petroleum Ministry (from $4.5 to $3/MMBtu) — i.e. it is confirmed to BE a natural-gas industrial customer, corroborating the second pass's 'two factories' framing and confirming this is the EDFU paper mill (not Qus, which the second-pass researcher was right to flag as a distinct town/mill and which this pass found no evidence links to this line). Sugar factory background (Ahram Gate / elbalad 4716538, not cited in output as redundant with already-verified refs): est. 1962, ~112,000 t/y, one of Upper Egypt's largest.

IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION this pass caught: the second pass's ElBalad/Ahram-Gate 'sugar factory operating on natural gas' framing needs a correction. Re-reading dostor.org/5268857 in full (fetched directly, not just via search snippet) shows the Aswan governor's remarks about converting 'مصنع السكر' from bagasse to natural gas are made explicitly in the context of 'أهالى مركز ومدينة كوم أمبو' (residents of Kom Ombo center/city) and immediately follow a sentence about a 22km west-bank-to-east-bank gas crossing serving Kom Ombo — i.e. this is the KOM OMBO sugar factory, a SEPARATE facility from the Edfu sugar factory (Upper Egypt Sugar & Integrated Industries operates multiple mills: Edfu, Kom Ombo, Armant, etc.). Do not conflate the two in any future write-up. This does NOT affect the Edfu sugar-factory gas connection (independently documented by argaam 1058075, youm7 5785120/6833618, cited unchanged from pass 2) — it only corrects which factory the dostor/governor's-tour quote describes.

Useful incidental confirmation from the same dostor article: the governor references 'استكمال مسافة 22 كم الخاصة بمسار توصيل الغاز الطبيعى من الجانب الغربى للنيل إلى الجانب الشرقى' (completing a 22km stretch of the gas delivery route from the WEST side of the Nile to the EAST side) for the Kom Ombo connection — independent confirmation that the GASCO Dahshour–Aswan trunk in this stretch runs along the west-desert side of the Nile, consistent with the main session's computed trunk geometry (west of the river, ~28-30km out). Also found: OSM/Overpass shows a numbered desert trunk highway ('طريق الاقصر, اسوان الغربى', ref 35 — the Luxor–Aswan Western Road) running through the box around the trunk's nearest-approach point to Edfu; GASCO transmission lines commonly parallel such desert highway rights-of-way, but this is inference/context, not a citable station name, and is NOT proposed as a coordinate source.

=== (a) TRUNK TIE-IN — STILL UNRESOLVED, dead ends this pass ===
1. Re-read youm7 2022-06-01 Edfu gas-startup photo essay (5785120) via full fetch (not just prior pass's snippet read): confirms general water/sewage/gas infrastructure completion timeline (July 2022), officials (Gov. Ashraf Attia, Arab Contractors CEO Sayed Farouk), 30-40M EGP budgets — but contains NO station/valve-room/km-point naming and NO mention of either factory. Dead end, do not re-read again.
2. Arabic search sweep (all separate queries, all came back empty/irrelevant for a named Edfu-spur tie-in): محطة غاز إدفو، خط غاز إدفو، غرفة بلوف إدفو، توصيل الغاز الطبيعي إدفو حياة كريمة، "نقطة توصيل"/"نقطة اتصال" الغاز الطبيعي إدفو خط دهشور، "محطة تخفيض ضغط" إدفو غاز مصر أسوان، "خط الصعيد" الغاز إدفو أسوان جاسكو، "دراسة تقييم الأثر البيئي" خط غاز إدفو أسوان, Petrojet إدفو خط أنابيب غاز. All either return the same already-cited youm7/elbalad/ahram/dostor set, generic/unrelated hits (Fayoum PRS, New Valley PRS, EIA boilerplate), or nothing.
3. NEW lead, not conclusive: youm7 2025-09-12 (7119475) reports a natural-gas line fire in Edfu city, located 'منطقة الكلح غرب، وتحديدًا بجوار المعهد الأزهرى' ('Al-Kolh West area, specifically next to the Azhar Institute'). Nominatim only resolves a 'الكلح شرق' (Al-Kolh East) village node (25.0874N/32.8427E, ~5km north of the sugar-factory node, west of Edfu city) — no 'Al-Kolh West' feature is separately mapped, and the article gives no further station name. This reads as a LOCAL DISTRIBUTION line incident (civil-defense response, no transmission/PRS terminology), not evidence of the 37km spur's trunk-side tie-in. Flagged for a future pass only if 'Al-Kolh' recurs in a more technical source; not used as a coordinate.
4. GASCO/Egypt Oil & Gas transmission maps: found only the general Dahshour–Aswan phase breakdown (Dahshour→Koriamat→Beni Suef→Abu Qirqas→Asyut→Girga→Aswan) with no Edfu-area station granularity; the Egypt Oil & Gas 'Egypt Gas Transmission Infrastructure Map' page did not yield accessible station-level detail via search/fetch.
5. Confirmed there are exactly 4 pressure-reduction & measurement stations across Aswan governorate (dostor 5268857: 'ضمن 4 محطات على مستوى المحافظة'), of which Kom Ombo's is one, DEFINITIVELY RULED OUT again this pass by distance (unchanged from pass 2: Kom Ombo town ~57km from Edfu, geometrically impossible for a 37km line). This implies a dedicated Edfu-area station almost certainly exists among the remaining 3, but no source names or locates it.
6. Confirmed (again, unchanged) that Kom Ombo TOWN remains ruled out. No new candidate for the actual named tie-in station was found.

RECOMMENDATION: leave end lon/lat null per hard rule (no fabricated coordinates). resolved=false. The main session should proceed with its own trunk-derived anchor for the end point as planned; if a fourth pass is warranted, the highest-value next step is NOT another web search sweep (this one is close to saturated for Arabic online news coverage) but a direct records request/FOIA-style approach: GASCO/EGAS as-built network GIS layer, an EEAA-approved EIA for this specific spur (search the eeaa.gov.eg project-status portal by project name rather than search engine), or a Petroleum Ministry official-gazette right-of-way decree, none of which are readily search-indexed.

start.coord_basis: Town centroid of Edfu/Idfu, Aswan Governorate — an independently geocodable Nile-valley town (reused from prior sweep); corroborated by three independent sources (Argaam, Youm7 2022, Al-Masry Al-Youm) describing the 37km/12in GASCO line delivering gas to Edfu's sugar/paper factories and households

end.name: UNRESOLVED — no source names the specific valve-room/tie-in point where the 37km Edfu spur leaves the GASCO Dahshour–Aswan ('Upper Egypt'/'South Valley') transmission trunk. The only concrete named candidate found — a real, SCADA-controlled gas pressure-reduction & metering station at Kom Ombo (confirmed by Ahram Gate + ElBalad; ElBalad states it supplies Edfu, Nasr al-Nuba, and Kom Ombo) — is DEFINITIVELY RULED OUT: Kom Ombo town (24.467N, 32.950E per Wikipedia) is ~57km straight-line from Edfu (24.9781N, 32.8749E), which is geometrically impossible for a 37km pipeline to span. The true tie-in must be much closer to Edfu than Kom Ombo, but no source names it.
end.coord_basis: No independently geocodable tie-in point identified — standing rule against fabricating or substituting an unconfirmed location

prior_passes.notes: Retry pass upgrades the prior researcher's evidence but does not resolve the tie-in. Two NEW sources this pass: ElBalad (elbalad.news/6735224) profiles a real, named, SCADA-controlled gas pressure-reduction & metering station at Kom Ombo (120M EGP, 2,500 sqm, 20,000 m3/h capacity) and explicitly states it serves >200,000 residents across Edfu, Nasr al-Nuba, and Kom Ombo (25,000 customers, 'Decent Life' initiative); Ahram Gate (gate.ahram.org.eg/News/5306934.aspx) independently confirms the Aswan governor touring this same 'محطة تخفيض ضغط وقياس الغاز الطبيعى' at Kom Ombo. This is a stronger, more specific candidate than the prior pass had (which only had loose 'Kom Ombo is nearby' reasoning) — BUT plugging in verified real-world coordinates (Kom Ombo town 24.467N/32.950E vs Edfu 24.9781N/32.8749E) shows they are ~57km apart in a straight line, which a 37km pipeline cannot span. This definitively rules out Kom Ombo TOWN as the tie-in (previously only flagged as a 'loose bound' at an incorrectly-estimated 15-20km). The station described in ElBalad may be a genuinely real GASCO/Egypt Gas asset that supplies Edfu via LOCAL distribution mains (a separate lower-pressure layer, not necessarily sited in Kom Ombo town itself, and not necessarily the point where the 37km TRANSMISSION spur taps the trunk) — so the actual physical location of whatever station serves this role could be well north of Kom Ombo town, closer to Edfu, but no source pins that location. Recommend leaving at ROUTE_PARTIAL (corridor-only) pending a GASCO network map or tender document naming the tie-in station explicitly; RouteAccuracy capped at 'low'.
